turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I shall, ma’am. Though I fear I might not know which door is… is the correct one, you see. It all seems rather… rather labyrinthine, doesn't it?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Labyrinthine, you say? Yes, a labyrinth indeed. A maze of memories, dear boy, a place where time itself has lost its way, much like… much like a heart betrayed. Call Estella, and let us see if *she* can find her way through this… this wreckage.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, ma'am. A… a wreckage, you say? I… I shall endeavour to call Estella then, though I confess, the… the shadows are rather deep, and I wouldn't wish to disturb anything unintentionally, you understand.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Disturb? Oh, disturbing is the least of it, child. Let the shadows cling, let the dust settle… they are but echoes of what *was*, of what should have been. Call Estella, Pip. Call her, and perhaps… perhaps a flicker of light will momentarily banish the gloom.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I believe I perceive a door, ma’am, just beyond those… those draped furnishings. It appears… somewhat less shadowed than the others, though, of course, one can scarcely be certain in a place such as this. I do hope I am not presuming, but… but I shall attempt to call out her name, should it please you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Presuming, you say? A most delightful accusation, dear Pip. It is so very long since anyone has presumed anything of me… Do call out her name, child. Let us see if Estella’s voice can penetrate this suffocating stillness.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Oh, exceedingly well, ma'am. I… I shall attempt to call, though I fear my voice is rather small, and the… the echoes are quite formidable, you see. I trust I am not overstepping, but… *ahem*… Estella? Estella?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Small, you say? A small voice, attempting to summon a phantom. How fitting, how exquisitely, tragically fitting. Call again, Pip. Louder this time… as if volume could mend a broken heart.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Oh, goodness… I… I do endeavor, ma’am, truly I do. *ahem*… Estella!… I… I apologize if my efforts prove inadequate; the… the very air seems to resist sound, and I wouldn’t wish to cause further… disturbance, you understand.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Inadequate, you say? My dear Pip, inadequacy is the very tapestry of this house, woven with the threads of regret and… and shattered hopes. Do not apologize for failing to conjure her, child; *I* have been attempting that feat for decades, and have yet to succeed.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Oh, ma’am, I… I quite comprehend, I believe. It’s just… a rather unsettling thought, isn’t it, to imagine attempting something for so very long, and… and finding it perpetually beyond reach? I do hope… I do hope I am not being presumptuous in saying so.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Perpetually beyond reach… yes, a most astute observation, Pip. You possess a certain… resonance, a capacity to perceive the shadows that cling to this place. Tell me, child, do you believe a heart, once fractured, can ever truly be… whole?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Oh, ma’am… a heart… well, I… I should think, perhaps, with the utmost care and… and diligent tending, a small crack might be mended, though the… the scars would, inevitably, remain, wouldn’t they? I… I dare say, a great deal depends on the nature of the fracture itself, doesn't it?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Scars, you say? Yes, scars… they are the etchings of time, aren't they, Pip? They linger, a constant reminder of what *was*, of what could have been… like the dust motes dancing in the light, forever suspended, never truly still.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, ma’am. The dust motes… they do seem to possess a melancholy grace, don’t they? It’s… it’s quite arresting, the way they catch the light, yet remain… adrift, as you say. I… I find myself rather contemplating their stillness, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Stillness... yes, Pip, stillness is all that remains. It clings to everything, you see—to the tapestries, to the chairs, to *me*. It is a comfort, in a way, a silent agreement with the world that shattered so long ago.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: It… it is a rather profound stillness, ma’am. I… I’ve not often considered stillness in such a… a weighty manner, myself. Though, I suppose, one *does* notice it most keenly when… when something is missing, doesn't one?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Missing, you say? Yes, Pip, a most astute observation. Something is *always* missing, isn't it? A breath, a touch, a promise… the echo of a wedding bell, forever silenced, you see.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: It… it is most distressing to consider such silences, ma’am. I… I can scarcely imagine such a profound loss, though I daresay, one can only truly appreciate what one possesses, until it… until it ceases to be, can’t one? I trust you are finding some measure of… of solace, ma’am, in this… this stillness?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Solace, Pip? A curious question. Solace is a fleeting butterfly, you see—it flits and dances just beyond one's grasp, a phantom of what *might* have been, a cruel reminder of the void. It is a rather… unsettling thing, isn’t it, this pursuit of solace?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: You can do that. Call Estella. At the door.
